program_level.business_purpose: This appears to be a claims processing and management system, likely for insurance or workers compensation claims. The program handles claim entry, validation, revision, and status tracking with an interactive panel-based interface.
program_level.data_flows: The program processes claim records with extensive data fields including social security numbers, filing dates, claim status, injury dates, settlement info, and medical totals. It uses a 1920-character panel record structure for display/input and maintains claim data with multiple date and status fields. The flow appears to be: read claim data -> display/edit via panels -> validate -> update records.
business_rules: Claim number validation and verification rules
Date validation rules for injury, filing, and settlement dates
Status progression rules for claim lifecycle management
Authorization/access control rules for address and injury date modifications
Business validation rules for record creation vs revision
Sequential record navigation and browsing rules
program_level.complexity_reasoning: The program exhibits high complexity due to: 1) Large size (12,562 lines, 828 paragraphs) 2) Complex UI interaction logic with multiple function keys and panels 3) Extensive business validation rules 4) Multiple data format conversions 5) Complex state management for claim processing 6) Integration with multiple external systems 7) Security/authorization requirements
program_level.recommendations: Consider breaking this monolithic application into smaller microservices: 1) Claim Data Service 2) Validation Service 3) UI Service 4) Authorization Service. Use Spring Boot for backend services, modern web framework for UI. Implement event-driven architecture for claim status changes. Consider gradual migration starting with read-only functions first.
